config.title: Build a weather dashboard using public API

intro.title: Build a weather dashboard using public API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple weather dashboard that fetches and displays current weather data for a city. You will learn how to make HTTP requests to a public weather API using JavaScript's Fetch API. The core programming concepts involved are asynchronous JavaScript, handling API responses, and dynamically updating the DOM with the retrieved data. You'll work with JSON data, event listeners for user input, and basic HTML/CSS to structure and style the dashboard. By the end, you'll have a functional web app that shows temperature, conditions, and other weather details.
intro.usecase: This pattern of fetching and displaying live data from a public API is the foundation of countless real-world dashboards. Developers use it to build weather apps like AccuWeather or The Weather Channel, financial dashboards showing stock prices, and live sports scoreboards. As a developer, you'll implement similar logic to create interactive admin panels that monitor system metrics, e-commerce product feeds, or social media feeds that update in real-time. Mastering this skill allows you to connect any frontend application to dynamic, external data sources.

objectives: Initialize and configure an API request to fetch weather data
Implement error handling for API responses and network failures
Construct a dashboard layout to display weather information
Manipulate DOM elements to render dynamic weather data
Integrate user input controls to search for different locations
Apply data transformation to format API responses for display
Bind event listeners to interactive dashboard components

steps.title: Import fetch API and create main function
steps.instruction: Create a function named getWeatherData that will fetch weather information. This function should be declared with the async keyword since it will make an API call.
steps.hint: Start with 'async function getWeatherData() {}' or 'const getWeatherData = async () => {}' to create an asynchronous function.

steps.title: Define function to fetch weather data from API
steps.instruction: Inside the WeatherDashboard component, create an async function named getWeatherData that takes a city parameter and uses fetch to get weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API.
steps.hint: Use the fetch API with the OpenWeatherMap endpoint (e.g., https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q={city}&appid={API_KEY}). Remember to use async/await and handle the response with .json().
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async getWeatherData function that uses fetch to retrieve weather data from the OpenWeatherMap API.
successCriteria: The getWeatherData function is defined inside the WeatherDashboard component, is async, takes a city parameter, uses fetch with the OpenWeatherMap API endpoint, and returns the parsed JSON data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is async, uses fetch with the correct API endpoint, and properly handles the response with .json().
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to be defined correctly. Remember to create an async function named getWeatherData that uses fetch to call the OpenWeatherMap API.
